# The Slash — Selection and Co-presence

## #0 — Specify what the stroke does

The inputs are two distinguishable terms and a field in which either can be selected. `/` carries two native operations: **OR** makes a determinate selection; **AND** retains the relation in which the alternatives belong together. The [slash root](../../the-slash.md) grounds their whole-bearing office. The [core theorem spine](../../episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy.md), §IV, sources the formal account.

## #1 — Selection requires alternatives

A computation selecting `0` or `1` makes one value actual in its specified operation. The two values remain distinguishable possibilities under the rule that selects them. Naming the selected value does not by itself record the field, criterion, or exclusions through which it was selected.

This is OR's exact office in the native account: a difference becomes available for determinate action. It does not by itself constitute the complete account of the act of distinction.

## #2 — Co-presence retains the field

AND holds the alternatives in one relation. Their coexistence as possibilities does not require both to be the selected output of a single ordinary Boolean computation. The native operation preserves the field through the distinction that makes an output possible.

`AND/OR` consequently names a paired relational demand rather than a new truth table silently replacing conjunction or disjunction. An external logical calculus must state its own propositions, values, connectives, and entailment relation before comparison.

## #3 — Work the two orientations

Applied to `0/1`, the stroke keeps the ground-through-expression reading together with the inverse `1/0`. Applied again, it gives `(0/1)/(1/0)`. The outer slash acts upon two complete first-order relations.

[The primordial-symbolon derivation](primordial-symbolon.md) extends the four slash-forms and retained pair. The arithmetic seam remains exact: ordinary `1/0` has no value. QL's relational operation uses that seam to make return towards the unobjectifiable ground visible.

## #4 — Distinguish neighbouring strokes

A division bar, a quotient by an equivalence relation, a Sheffer stroke, and the native AND/OR share graphical possibilities without sharing one universal operation. Division requires a specified algebraic domain; quotient construction requires an equivalence relation or action; a Sheffer stroke has its specified truth-functional definition.

[The formal-neighbour register](../formal-neighbours/README.md) extends those comparisons. The present record keeps the native primitive answerable by stating its own inputs and result: selected difference with the field of co-presence retained.

## #5→0 — A determination can return

A result carrying its selection and relation can be reconsidered when its conditions change. The [Dia/Syn folder](../dia-syn/README.md) extends the productive and collapsed accountings of this operation.

This record returns-to [A13](../../../section-rooms/arguments/A13-Two-Logics-of-Two-Dia-Syn.md), [A18](../../../section-rooms/arguments/A18-Primordial-Symbolon-and-Its-Eight-Determinations.md), and [Movement21, Sym-Ballein](../../../section-rooms/03-two-logics/movements/21-s2-p2-sym-ballein.md). Its formal result is the retained possibility of reading the determination through the relation it has made actual.
